notes.text: The sheet has no separate authorial page number. The formulas are visibly labelled (49) and (50); the thin, lighter 75 at the lower-left edge is foliation in another hand. The opening d=delta(i), d-prime=delta(j) definitions are crossed out. The labels are reported from this page alone, without using H's editorial reference to an earlier leaf.

For i<j the manuscript writes Sigma_ij as the intersection of dotted T_i and Sigma_j and then gives two rows of expressions for a flag. The ensuing prose says that the cofinal inclusions of flags have transition morphisms de façon évidente, and describes the general-inclusion definitions as depending on a choice of retractions. These are the author's statements; no proof was checked in this transcription pass.

The manuscript writes T_i^(d)=T_i cap X^(d), d=delta(i), then an X expression whose first subscript remains i/j. Its following inclusion-and-map chain ends at X_i^(d)=Sigma_i. The complete structure is represented by the written tuple and a fork from Sigma_ij to upper Sigma_j and lower Sigma_i. No equality or equivalence beyond the written symbols has been inferred.

The final parenthesis says that equisingularity hypotheses and a condition de locale trivialité on the retractions are required for the final Sigma expressions to be fibrations. The carrier glyph after stratification de is kept as alpha-leading/X-alternative from its closed left loop and two right arms. The final connector is the written plain shaft; these readings do not supply a theorem or repair the displayed data.

The continuation clusters are transcribed occurrence by occurrence: two strokes in the prose flag and in the raised entre les index, point plus two strokes in the source index of (50) and its second-row continuation, and point plus one stroke in the first row. There is no additional cap before the second-row continuation or an extra comparison angle after i_1 in the flag. The manuscript's unequal graphical forms are retained without assigning new operations to them.

The heavy cancellations leave the first dotted-T/index group of (49), morphismes, the small f/t glyph and the lower fib/f fragment uncertain. The latter includes a detached point and tall right remnant, so the cancellation is not silently reduced to a certain single letter. The lower sur les is attached by its curved leader after i.e. before the second T; the larger locale insertion is attached after condition.

At the right edge of the fork, the outer closing parenthesis has only upper and lower surviving curve ends, retained as an uncertain typeset parenthesis with the crop loss described. Four aligned final points are followed spatially by a separate lower-left dark speck, whose function is left unassigned. H's initial editorial note, formula-number comment and final section heading are not source writing on this leaf and are excluded from textual-change counts.
